title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Ava Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise customer onboarding, integration validation, operational health checks, Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), and escalations. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and Platform owners. Follow the documented steps to ensure consistent time-to-value, predictable launches, and a clear escalation path when incidents or regressions occur.

Scope

- Applies to enterprise customers (Dedicated, Private, and high-commit Hosted accounts).
- Covers pre-sales-to-production handoff, technical integration checklist, first 90 days of health checks, QBR cadence & templates, and the escalation matrix.
- Does not replace product release notes or platform-specific runbooks; links to those sources are included.

Owner & Contacts

- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Ava Patel)
- SE lead (integration): Michael Chen
- Support lead (priority escalations): Sara López

Section A — Enterprise Onboarding: phases and checklist

Intro: Onboarding is divided into Discovery, Integrate & Validate, Pilot & Tune, and Production Rollout. Each phase has clear acceptance criteria and owners.

Phase 1 — Discovery (owner: CS/AE)
1. Kickoff meeting (agenda pinned to kickoff template): participants: customer PM, infra, security, SE, CS.
2. Success criteria: latency SLOs, throughput targets, data residency, compliance controls, expected monthly token volume.
3. Risk review: sensitive data requirements, audit/KMS needs, network topology constraints.

Phase 2 — Integrate & Validate (owner: SE)
1. Integration checklist: complete the items in the Integration Requirements table (below).
2. Provide sample requests and SDK examples; validate end-to-end request flow to Redwood API / private endpoint.
3. Run baseline performance tests: 95th percentile latency, per-second throughput, error rate < 1% for integration traffic.

Phase 3 — Pilot & Tune (owner: SE + CS)
1. Pilot period (2–4 weeks typical): monitor cost per token, latency, and output quality against acceptance criteria.
2. Apply batching & cache recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
3. Capture prompt set and evaluation metrics; flag regression thresholds for rolling back model changes.

Phase 4 — Production Rollout (owner: CS + Customer Ops)
1. Cutover plan: DNS/endpoint switch schedule, rollback window (48 hours recommended), and communication plan.
2. Post-cutover checks: traffic validation, error monitoring, initial QPS sample.
3. Handoff to Support and account-level operations for ongoing QBRs.

Integration Requirements (table)
| Requirement | Details / Acceptable values | Owner | Validation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Endpoint type | hosted / dedicated / private (VPC) | SE | Successful request to endpoint with sample payload |
| Auth | API key or mTLS depending on deployment | SE/Security | Authenticated request returns 200 |
| Network | IP allowlist, VPC peering, or private link | Customer infra + SE | Connectivity test (curl/openssl) |
| Data handling | KMS/HSM requirement, retention window | CS + Security | Signed data handling agreement |
| SLO targets | 95th latency ms, availability % | CS + Customer | Baseline test report attached |
| Observability | Export spans/logs to customer's observability tool (optional) | SE + Eng-Platform | Traces visible in customer's APM

Note: For Private deployments include onprem-packaging checklist from eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures.

Code snippets / example request
- REST curl (hosted API):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

Section B — Known Issues & Workarounds (tracked items)

- Issue: Intermittent 503s during high burst traffic on Dedicated pools.
  - Symptom: Short-lived 503s for subset of requests during autoscale.
  - Temporary workaround: Retry with exponential backoff (recommended initial backoff 200ms, max 2s).
  - Long-term: SE to open Capacity request with eng-infra to increase burst headroom for account during business hours.

- Issue: Tokenization mismatch between SDK versions.
  - Symptom: Off-by-one token counts leading to prompt truncation.
  - Workaround: Pin SDK to supported version listed in eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides and re-tokenize historical prompts.

- Issue: Private deployment networking changes cause loss of connectivity after kernel/agent restarts.
  - Workaround: Follow onprem-packaging/upgrade-and-rollback network validation checklist and restart agent with --reconnect flag.

Section C — Escalation Playbook

Purpose: Provide a clear, time-bound escalation path for customer-impacting issues (severity P0–P2).

Severity definitions
- P0 (SEV0): Total service outage preventing production traffic, major data loss or security incident.
- P1 (SEV1): Degraded service impacting critical customer flows (large % of requests failing or latency SLOs broken).
- P2 (SEV2): Functional issues with limited scope or workaround available.

Escalation matrix (summary)
- Triage: Support on first call (Slack #support-enterprise), open incident in incident tracker (link to oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process).
- If P0: immediate page to SRE + Eng Serving Runtime + CS Director. Page sequence: oncall SRE -> runtime engineer -> CS Director.
- If P1: page Support lead -> SE lead -> SRE on-call (if not resolved in 30 mins).

Contacts (example)
- Support queue: support-enterprise@redwood.ai (monitored 24/7)
- SE lead: Michael Chen (michael@redwood.ai)
- SRE on-call: see eng-sre/capacity-planning on-call roster
- CS Director: Sarah Kim (sarah@redwood.ai)

Escalation steps (numbered)
1. Triage & notify: Support opens incident, notes severity, ETA for initial patch.
2. Mobilize: If P0/P1 escalate within 10 minutes to on-call SRE and SE lead.
3. Bridge & updates: Create a persistent conference bridge and post updates every 15 minutes for P0.
4. Postmortem: For P0/P1, owner (SRE + SE) to own postmortem within 72 hours and publish to oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems.

Section D — First 90-day Health Checks & Signals

Weekly check (first month)
- Metrics to review: request volume by endpoint, 95th & 99th percentile latency, error rates by status code, model output quality score (from evals).
- Logs/traces: sample traces for requests above 95th percentile latency.
- Cost: monthly projected cost-vs-budget; flag >10% variance.

Monthly check (month 2–3)
- Validate rollout of batching & cache settings; review Redwood Optimize suggestions applied.
- Security & compliance: verify audit logs, KMS rotation, and retention policies.
- Customer health survey: survey score and open action items.

Signal thresholds to alert CS/SE
- Latency: 95th latency exceeds target by 30% for >30 minutes.
- Errors: sustained error rate >1% for 15 minutes.
- Cost: daily spend exceeds projected burn rate by 25%.

Section E — QBR Template & Agenda

Cadence: Quarterly (first QBR at 6–8 weeks post-production). Participants: CS, SE, Product, Engineering stakeholder from customer.

Standard QBR agenda
1. Executive summary (CS) — current state, usage highlights, key wins.
2. Health dashboard review (SE) — performance, errors, cost.
3. Quality & model updates (Applied ML) — evaluation results, regressions.
4. Roadmap & requests (Product) — feature asks, priority backlog.
5. Risk & action plan (CS) — open items and owners.
6. Next steps & commitments.

Deliverables before QBR (owner)
- Health dashboard link (SE)
- Top 10 prompt evals and quality metrics (Applied ML)
- Cost summary and optimization opportunities (Finance/CS)
